Latin word

ferē

ferē (fermē)

adverb, usually after the word it qualifies

nearly, about; nearly, almost; with a negative, hardly any; generally, usually; as a rule, usually; with numbers, about

In this lexicon

  • about

    also used · classical · Traupman 202

  • almost

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.15: nihil ferē intellegit (Lewis & Short); Cic. Mur. 6: nēmō ferē saltat sōbrius (Lewis & Short, by chapter); Traupman 26: nihil ferē, practically nothing

  • in general

    also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 6.10: fit ferē ut (Lewis & Short); Traupman 98; Traupman 98: ferē, vulgō

  • usually

    also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 363–364: rūrī ferē sē continēbat; Sen. Ep. 53.1: quae ferē aut in aquam aut in ventum resolvuntur

Examples

  • Haec ferē dīxit.

    He said something like this.Traupman 102

    In the entry for about

  • pauper, cui opera vīta erat, rūrī ferē sē continēbat

    being poor, with only his work to live on, he usually kept to the countryTer. Ph. 363–364
